title: ATO to update existing LRBA guidance
full_text:
The ATO has confirmed it will be providing the sector with updated guidance on the new limited recourse borrowing arrangement (LRBA) rules in the immediate future.
“We [already] have some rulings, SMSFR 2012/1 on limited recourse borrowing arrangements and SMSFR 2009/1 on what is considered business real property. Both those rulings are expected to be published with some LRBA updates later this month and will go out for public consultation,” ATO SMSF branch director Kellie Grant told delegates at the SMSF Trustee Empowerment Day 2026, co-hosted by smstrusteenews and the SMSF Association in Sydney on Tuesday.
“So hopefully by the end of this month you will see a little bit more guidance on this issue from us.”
In addition to these enhanced instruments, Grant pointed out trustees can access QC107811 on the ATO website as another LRBA information resource.
She also took the opportunity to outline the steps trustees should follow now when considering to use an LRBA to acquire a business real property asset for their SMSF.
“For trustees now considering [using a limited recourse] borrowing arrangement, the practical starting point is to ask several questions,” she suggested.
“[The first is] does the property satisfy the definition of business real property? That means the property is used wholly and exclusively in one or more businesses and the business obviously doesn’t have to be run by the SMSF.
“Also ask the questions: do you have documentation supporting that position, have you considered how the property is being used, how it’s expected to be used in the future, would an independent person viewing the arrangement, such as your fund auditor, reach the same conclusion?”
She specifically recommended particular care be taken where a property combining commercial and residential use is being sought, and also with vacant properties between tenants, property development activities and where there is a short-term change in the use of the premises.
